turns.content: Identify the Standard Model gauge factors SU(3)C, SU(2)L, and U(1)Y. Why must 'approximation precision' specify a metric, topology, and target?

Adopt a criterion in which the admissible discrete approximants must have covering radius tending to zero throughout each full target identified above. Why is matching only a restricted observable class insufficient?
For the U(1) target identified above, construct an admissible family of finite subgroups and determine how their neighbouring angular spacing changes with order.
Apply the same full-target criterion to the remaining targets using their finite-family classification or local structure.
Under the full-target covering-radius criterion, which gauge factor permits arbitrarily precise approximation by finite subgroups?
State explicitly that the conclusion is conditional on that adopted criterion.
If approximation were required only for class functions rather than throughout the group, how would the conclusion change?
Report which target admits the finite family, describe that family, and state the qualification on the approximation criterion.
